Lunch is a traditional mixed grill; you return to Cairo in the afternoon.

itinerary.title: Cairo arrival and Giza plateau
itinerary.source: After the airport transfer, the first full afternoon goes to the Giza plateau — the Great Pyramid of Khufu, the Pyramid of Khafre, the Pyramid of Menkaure, and the Great Sphinx crouched below them.

itinerary.title: Alexandria: the Mediterranean detour
itinerary.source: Day two takes the desert highway north to Alexandria — the city Alexander the Great founded in 331 BC and that became, under the Ptolemies, the intellectual capital of the ancient world.

itinerary.title: Memphis, Saqqara and Dahshur pyramid sequence
itinerary.source: The third day reaches back to the beginning of pyramid-building — which is to say, to the beginning of large stone construction anywhere on earth.

itinerary.title: Flight to Luxor, East Bank
itinerary.source: A morning flight south carries you to Luxor — ancient Thebes, the religious capital of the New Kingdom pharaohs — and the city deserves two full days.

itinerary.title: Luxor West Bank, Valley of the Kings
itinerary.source: The second Luxor day crosses to the land of the dead.

itinerary.title: Road to Aswan via Edfu, Kom Ombo
itinerary.source: Day six is a travelling day in the best sense.

itinerary.title: Abu Simbel and Aswan
itinerary.source: The seventh day is the longest of the tour and, for most travellers, the most extraordinary.

itinerary.title: Flight to Cairo, Coptic quarter, bazaar
itinerary.source: A flight north returns you to Cairo, and the day is given to the city's older layers.

itinerary.title: The museum chapter
itinerary.source: The ninth day is the museum chapter, and it is a full one.

itinerary.title: Airport transfer
itinerary.source: The airport transfer follows the next morning, with later departures readily accommodated.
